title: Pricing Velocity Triggered Headcount Simulator - Nov 2026
content:
Objective:
Short simulation sheet to estimate headcount and budget impact from pricing changes that alter customer request velocity (peakiness) rather than just volume. Use this to stress-test burst coverage and soft-commit hiring triggers for Dedicated and Hosted lanes.

Context / motivation:
- Commercial feedback: small price-per-token increases on heavy customers can change their batching patterns and request frequency (more small requests vs fewer large ones).
- Traditional unit-econ sensitivity focuses on avg tokens/month. This simulator models how request velocity (requests/minute distribution) affects GPU session churn, KV cache effectiveness, and therefore hourly cost and effective throughput per engineer.

High-level assumptions (base case = A):
- Base monthly tokens: 45B tokens (company-wide).
- Base requests/day: 54M requests (avg request size = 830 tokens).
- Avg sequence length when hit cache: 600 tokens; effective cache reuse reduces per-token cost by 18% at baseline.
- GPU mix cost (weighted avg) = $2.10 / GPU-hour (includes infra and ops)
- Serving throughput baseline: 200k tokens/GPU-hour (after batching & KV reuse)
- Ops per hire (SWE infra) supports 25% token growth before a hire required; on-call coverage and rota require 1 SRE per 12 reserved clusters.

Key engineered variables (what we vary):
- price_delta_pct: customer-facing price change that drives request pattern (e.g., +8% => customers split larger requests into more interactive smaller calls)
- velocity_shift_factor: multiplier on requests/day (if >1, more small requests; if <1, fewer larger ones)
- avg_tokens_per_request: inverse of velocity (smaller tokens per request when velocity higher)
- cache_hit_delta: change in KV/prefix cache reuse (higher velocity -> lower reuse)
- batching_efficiency: fraction of ideal GPU throughput achieved (drops when velocity increases)
- soft_commit_threshold: reserved capacity utilization % above which we trigger hiring or burst-capacity contracts

Scenario definitions:
- A: Baseline (price_delta_pct=0, velocity_shift_factor=1.0, avg_tokens_per_request=830, cache_hit_delta=0, batching_efficiency=1.0, soft_commit_threshold=0.75)
- B: Price hike leads to more interactive behavior (price_delta_pct=+10%, velocity_shift_factor=1.35, avg_tokens_per_request=615, cache_hit_delta=-0.12, batching_efficiency=0.86, soft_commit_threshold=0.70)
- C: Discount/feature -> batched usage (price_delta_pct=-6%, velocity_shift_factor=0.85, avg_tokens_per_request=970, cache_hit_delta=+0.08, batching_efficiency=1.08, soft_commit_threshold=0.80)
- D: Spike (unrelated product event) - 48hr surge (velocity_shift_factor=2.6, avg_tokens_per_request=420, cache_hit_delta=-0.22, batching_efficiency=0.62)

Quick calculation blocks (textual table):
Columns: scenario | monthly tokens | monthly requests | effective tokens/GPU-hr | GPU-hours needed | GPU cost/mo | ops hires needed | headcount-trigger note
- A | 45,000,000,000 | 1,620,000,000 | 200,000 | 225,000 | $472,500 | 0 | within soft_commit
- B | 45,000,000,000 | 2,187,000,000 | 172,000 | 261,628 | $549,420 | +3 contractors or 1 full-time ops hire | soft_commit breached at 72% utilization; recommend prebook 10% burst pool or trigger hire window
- C | 45,000,000,000 | 990,000,000 | 216,000 | 208,333 | $437,500 | - | headroom increases; consider converting burst budget to marketing credit
- D (48hr) | 3,000,000,000 tokens in surge window | 71,428,571 requests in 2 days | 124,000 | incremental 24,190 GPU-hrs over 2 days | $50,799 | emergency on-call activation (2x) | require rapid borrowing of burst capacity; recommend pre-approved overtime fund

Notes on formulas used (for transparency):
- monthly requests = (monthly tokens) / (avg_tokens_per_request)
- effective tokens/GPU-hr = baseline_throughput * batching_efficiency * (1 + cache_hit_delta)
- GPU-hours needed = monthly_tokens / effective_tokens/GPU-hr
- GPU cost/mo = GPU-hours_needed * GPU_hour_cost

Headcount triggers (proposal):
- Ops hire: if sustained utilization > soft_commit_threshold for 6+ weeks OR if GPU-hours needed delta > +12% month-over-month and projected monthly revenue drop < 6% from pricing changes.
- SWE infra hire: if model for request velocity shows sustained degradation in batching_efficiency causing >15% increase in operator toil (measured by incident minutes), hire 1 SWE per 15% efficiency delta.
- SRE on-call scaling: for every additional 120k reserved GPU-hours sustained, add 1 SRE to on-call roster.

Pricing sensitivity playbook (what finance & product should coordinate on):
1) Pre-change simulation: run scenario B and D with customer clusters known to be latency-sensitive.
2) Field experiment: A/B test +10% price on 3 mid-size customers and measure request fragmentation over 14 days. Stop if GPU-hours increase >10% or error rate rises.
3) Mitigations: bundle micro-batching incentives (discounts for larger single requests), or introduce slight per-request surcharge for sub-200-token requests for very high-throughput customers.
4) Capacity levers: shift affected traffic to Dedicated pools with pinned models (maintain KV reuse), enable burst credits, or promote quantized variants for best-effort traffic.

Risk table (qualitative):
- Repricing without velocity model -> hidden cost increases (medium-to-high)
- Customers shift to more frequent interactive calls -> SLO pressure on latency (high)
- Burst exposure during holidays -> operational fatigue, risk of SLA breaches (high)

Immediate asks / next steps: (owner: Aisha)
- Prioritize a 2-week A/B pilot with Product on +10% test (tickets: JIRA-FIN-3421).
- Engineering: instrument request-size histogram per-customer + KV-hit ratio delta; target: export daily to finance (owner: Evan).
- Finance: pre-approve $60k emergency burst fund for Q4 (owner: Miguel).
- People ops: hold a 30-day candidate pipeline for 1 infra SWE + 1 ops hire if pilot shows >8% sustained GPU-hours increase.

Appendix (observability hooks to capture):
- per-customer requests/min histogram (bucketed by token ranges)
- cache-hit ratio time series and fold by model version
- batch-size distribution and avg tokens/GPU-hr by cluster

Scratch calculations (for reviewer reproduction):
Baseline throughput math: 45e9 tokens / 200,000 tokens per GPU-hr = 225,000 GPU-hrs/mo.
Scenario B throughput math: effective throughput = 200k * 0.86 * (1 - 0.12) = ~172k; therefore GPU-hrs = 45e9 / 172k = ~261,628 GPU-hrs -> delta +16.3% -> incremental monthly GPU cost ~ $76,920 at $2.10/hr.

Document history & notes:
- Drafted 2026-11-05 after Q3 ops review.
- Reviewed with Product and Solutions Eng 2026-11-09.
- Requesting finance review and signoff on emergency burst budget by 2026-11-15.

Quick decision checklist (for on-call lead):
- Is utilization > soft_commit_threshold? If yes, notify finance and engage burst pool.
- Is cache-hit ratio degraded > 10% vs baseline? If yes, flag for model engineers.
- Is expected monthly cost delta > $50k? If yes, open hiring trigger discussion.

End of sheet.
